quotes.excerpt: White Boat #3 brings the series to a close with confidence, tying together its themes of guilt, control, and the unknown in a way that feels both unsettling and satisfying. Scott Snyder keeps the emotional core centered on Lee, giving his journey a sense of purpose even as the world around him spirals into chaos. The reveal of the island’s true nature adds weight to the story’s central ideas, while the final act pushes the horror into overdrive. Francesco Francavilla’s art elevates every moment, making the danger feel immediate and the environment oppressive. It is a finale that sticks with you, even as it leaves some of its mysteries lingering.

White Boat #3 is a fitting end to a wild story. The twist and turns keep you off the scent of how this story will actually end. However, once we enter the end game the issue picks up in the form of violence and action. The artwork is equally as good and competes with the story for the readers’ attention.

Seven issues in, End of Life continues to prove why it is one of the best comics of the year with its frantic energy, nihilistic humour and stylised artwork. This series keeps finding new ways to make the scenarios stranger and the characters even angrier at Eddie, all of them weaving in and out to create a truly chaotic yet entertaining story.

I know I sound like a broken record but I can’t stop singing this comic run its praises! Kyle Starks makes someone as unlikeable as Eddie Stallion a character you want to root for, and brings a compelling story along with him. This comic is a full course meal and only gets better and better.

No Gods, No Masters is proof that some of the best kaiju stories aren’t those solely about giant monsters tearing apart cities, but the ones about the people who are left in the aftermath. Julio Anta and Jacoby Salcedo have created an emotional, timely series that balances large scale destruction with heart. No Gods, No Masters is a monster story with tale that stands above the giants who have attacked the city.

No Gods No Masters issue number 1 is a masterclass in crafting a perfect fist issue! This story kicked off with a bang and I cannot wait to see where this series goes. The action, characters, and rich lore are immediately evident and each page is a work of art.

The Dirt Beneath the Devil #1 is an amazing opening issue for the series that will surely trap readers’ interest in reading more of the series. The mysteries that this issue either straight out tells us or implies are enough to peek even the most jaded readers’ interest. The premise that is laid out here in the first issue is intriguing, but when you know that Panosian obviously has more in store for us that jacks the intrigued levels all the way up. This should be a slam dunk pick up at the shop or Neon Ichiban this week. As a matter of fact, make sure to add this one to your Pull List as you won’t want to miss a single issue of this series.
The Dirt Beneath the Devil #1 is a solid debut issue. It takes a familiar concept and puts it in a setting that feels rather new and fresh.
Slowing down and giving Kyle the spotlight has been paying dividends so far as a great change of pace for a run that’s mostly delivered cosmic action up to this point.

A former flame burst back into Kyle’s life while Odyssey learns the high cost of fame! Adams takes Rayner and company into some wild spaces with the writing. The art teams deliver on the drama and craziness of mascots. Welcome to Hollywood, Kyle!

Space bandits Thena Khole and Cody Blue return in a new crossover series for the summer, Star-Crossed. Having stolen from a tyrannical monarchy, the girls just want to party. But any tyrant who’s been wronged is never going to let it go. And so the girls have a bounty on their heads they naively think they can escape. Best of luck, girls. From Mark Millar and Corrado Mastantuono.

Mark Millar delivers once again in this interstellar sci-fi outing any fan of the genre will love! Whether you’ve been following the Millarverse or not, this is one that any reader can easily get sucked into. Helped by the exceptional work of Corrado and Nisa Mastantuono, “Star-Crossed” is on its way to being one of the great modern sci-fi romps.

The Uncanny X-Men is going new places and doing things unlike ever before. There’s no other word to describe what Gail Simone and the creative team are doing other than “groundbreaking.” As always, I will be very anxiously waiting for the new issue to drop!

Gambit’s latest attempt to rid his curse becomes all too complicated in another great issue! Simone teases some future moments while pushing into the supernatural present. Vecchio and Wilson shine with the action panels and more personal looks. The team on UXM never fails on bringing out the best of the X-Men every time!

Conan The Barbarian #33 sets sail when Conan and the Red Brotherhood are shipwrecked on a mysterious island after encountering a massive storm and a supernatural attacker. Jim Zub’s start to the latest arc is as strong as ever, and Fernando Dagnino’s artwork is a perfect fit. 10 out of 10. No notes.

This is a ripping yard of piracy and sorcery, which highlights an often overlooked aspect of Conan’s background and the true character of Valeria of the Red Brotherhood. The artwork holds to the same standard of detail and drive. If you think of Conan as little more than a big, dumb barbarian, prepare to be educated!
G.I. Joe #25 is a major milestone done right, paying off years of buildup and kicking off the series' most epic storyline yet.

G.I. JOE #25 is a phenomenal start to the Nightforce story arc. Joshua Williamson, Tom Reilly and Andrea Milana pace things out that you feel like you are experiencing the start of a big blockbuster event. Everything that happens in this issue comes across as being a payoff for many sub-plots that have been developed since the start of the series. Where the payoff leads to is anyone’s guess, leaving you as the reader even more excited to find out what happens next.

The story is great, the art is stunning, and it’s a trial by fire for Superboy Prime that makes me more confident than ever that this character is actually here to stay. Just an amazing turnaround for this once-hated figure.

Superman #39 is a can’t-miss issue for this Spring’s biggest event. This issue sets up exciting new things for the DC Universe. This is an all-star creative team, and it feels like they are not holding back their talents at all with this arc.

Superman #40 is damn near perfect. This arc acted as a bit of a redemption for Superboy Prime and I absolutely adore him after this. Whilst the story here is wrapped up, this isn’t the last time we will see Superboy Prime and there seems to be a bright future ahead for him and his “supporting characters”.

This has been a phenomenal story setting up Prime’s future, but special credit once again goes to Dan Mora, who plays with the nature of the comic book format in some incredibly unique ways. The original Superman is back next month for the kickoff of the big “Kingdom of Zod” event, but I hope Williamson gets to keep writing Prime for a long time.

Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles #300 (#20) not only pushes the great story that we have been following forward, but also gives this milestone issue a big feel as well. The drama, action, surprises, and emotions are firing on all cylinders in this issue. If this issue doesn’t make you feel something you may need to check your pulse. They could’ve just phoned this one in as the 300th issue milestone is more than enough to sell the book. But they didn’t phone it in at all and crafted an issue that is sure to bring readers back next month for issue 21. If Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles is not on your Pull List already it needs to be added ASAP! If you are a comic book collector this 300th issue needs to be added to your collection as well. Cheers to 300 issues of TMNT and can’t wait for the 400th milestone issue!

This issue takes you on an emotional ride! Sure there is plenty of action within these pages. All while tugging at your heart strings with the current situation revolving around Shen. Losing a loved one and having the chance to bring them back is going to hit home with many readers I suspect. You do not want to miss out on this start of a new storyline for this series of TMNT. Go get your copy today!
Power Rangers Unlimited #1 is a bold, legacy embracing start which easily grabs hold of the best of BOOM!-era Power Rangers comics and presents it from a fresh and exciting angle.

Power Rangers Unlimited #1 delivers an action-packed debut that leans into Power Rangers history from a fresh point of view, and when combined with the out-of-this-world art and extensive roster, Power Rangers Unlimited becomes a must-read for any and every fan of the franchise.

Operation: Iron Coffin #2 keeps the momentum going with a bigger, bloodier, and more personal chapter for Dracula. Kenny Porter deepens the story without slowing down the action, while Tyrell Cannon’s artwork delivers the chaos, horror, and energy this concept demands. This series continues to be an absolute blast and remains an easy Pull List recommendation. Do not sleep on this series! Make sure you jump on this train now, as you don’t want to miss what happens next.

I don’t know how they’re doing it, but “Operation: Iron Coffin” is one of the best out this year. Kenny Porter manages to create a version of Dracula that feels relatable yet horrifying. His writing coupled with Cannon’s fantastic artwork create a truly amazing reading experience.
One of the best series in comics right now. The art is wild, creative, adventurous, and stunning. The story keeps drawing you back in issue after issue.
Marc Spector: Moon Knight #7 delivers an exhilarating ride with huge action, incredible artwork, and deadly stakes. It leaves you itching for the next issue.

The Smart Division is a fantastic science-fiction mystery that eerily could be more fact than fiction. Writer Zack Kaplan delivers a timely detective tale exploring the use of modern technology in solving crimes. However, it’s the juxtaposition of John Pearson’s elegant brush strokes that makes story rise above the rest. Kaplan and Pearson’s creativity knows no bounds and The Smart Division is proof of that.

I sat down with The Smart Division expecting a slick sci-fi detective story and walked away rattled about the world outside my window. That is the highest thing I can say about a comic right now. This is a perfect debut and one of the most relevant books on the stands, and I cannot wait to see where the case goes.

King Shazam and Superman throw down in a final fight for the ages! Arron leaves it all on table with the script. The art team never knows a ceiling in how far to raise the stakes. Highest possible recommendation.

Absolute Superman #21 feels like a true spectacle and lives up to the hype in every way as this arc comes to. a close. There is so much violence, emotion, and power packed into these pages that it may, in fact, be my favorite issue of the run yet.

Operation: Iron Coffin comes out of the gate swinging with a unique premise that delivers far more than ever expected. Kenny Porter and Tyrell Cannon give us a Dracula that isn’t just here for the carnage, although we get plenty of that, but for a compelling redemption arc wrapped in a fast-paced, blood-soaked WWII setting. IDW Dark may have some heavy hitting titles in its first year as an imprint at IDW Publishing, but Operation: Iron Coffin stands out as one of the best.

Operation Coffin #1 is a stylish debut for Porter and Cannon’s new take on Dracula. A truly unique premise, backed by engaging lore and a curious mission have already laid the groundwork for a wild ride ahead.

We get our first hints of how this fits in with the rest of the Absolute Universe just as it ends, but this feels much more like an evergreen, one-of-a-kind comic that people will be talking about for years.

Camp, Rodríguez and Otsmane-Elhaou leave readers with an intense read unlike anything else seen in the comics landscape currently. A phenomenal script gels perfectly with Rodríguez’s incredible art yet again. While its’ a bittersweet moment with the series on hold/over, readers leave with an overwhelming sense of the true direction of superhero comics for years to come. Highest possible recommendation.
Superman: The Stranger #1 returns to Clark Kent's roots, spinning a story that shows why Superman is such a timeless character.

The best Superman comic I’ve read in years!  A 1930s reinvention of the Man of Steel that returns Superman to his 1930s roots, but zigs and zags in ways you won’t expect, while keeping you on your toes. With a story that hooks you from the go and art and colours that leap off the page, this is a must-read mini-series.

The struggle between government and heroes in the 1950’s leads to a covert mission of grave stakes. Lemire stages the last hoorah with a script that never eases on pressure. Kristiansen & Guerrero give a cold look at the dark reality of secret heroics with excellent art. A timeless tale that won’t be soon forgotten.
These throwback issues looking at the Golden Age JSA are always a treat. This was a very entertaining start to this vintage arc.
Emperor Aquaman #21 finally gives us the big supervillain attack on Atlantis, and the results are both jaw-droppingly gorgeous and dramatically tense for Arthur and his kingdom

War has come to Atlantis and is taking no prisoners in this strong opening round. Adams pushes the conflict to dangerous levels with the writing. Timms, Lokus & Sharpe craft an explosive action sequence everywhere you turn! “The Tidal War” is a sure-fire, can’t miss event!
I probably sound like a broken record by now, but I can’t stop singing this comic run its praises. There’s so much to love about it and I look forward to each issue!

The Fury of Firestorm #6 closes the door on one chapter of the Nuclear Man's life, while opening the door to another. Out of all of DC's Next Level books, this has been one of the most surprising, and I can't wait to see what these final issues bring to the table.
Supergirl, Superboy, and Ursa arrive on Krypton prior to its explosion, but can Kara Zor-El truly stop Ursa from altering the past without being tempted to do the same herself?

Kara’s return to Krypton is anything but welcoming as Ursa attempts to rewrite the past! Campbell stages the heavy emotional weight with an excellent script. The art team crafts a steady look into the failing attempts of hope. There’s no telling how things are going to play out from here!

The Deadman #4 takes Boston Brand from Hell to Heaven and delivers another entertaining mix of supernatural mystery, dark comedy, and character development. W. Maxwell Prince continues to give Deadman a fresh voice, while Martin Morazzo and Chris O’Halloran make the afterlife visually unforgettable. The story moves the Mr. Juan mystery forward and finishes with a fantastic cliffhanger involving Swamp Thing and the “GR33N.”

Brand’s trip to Heaven is anything but divine as more problems arise. Prince adds in more out of place humor into events with the writing. Morazzo & O'Halloran keep steady with the presentation of art. Fearless in its’ delivery with a style all its’ own,

Quips and whips abound in this exellent entry of an already fun series! The fact that this team did brought back a character that I’ve been begging Marvel to bring back for nearly a decade is just the icing on the cake of this fantastic issue! Joshua Williamson, Carmen Carnero, and Nolan Woodard are doing the Lord’s work in bringing back the heart and essence of this long running franchise!

Tony’s got a case of deja vu with Whiplashes running wild! Williamson stacks the deck, leading to a major closing reveal. Carnero and the team keep the emotions high with stellar artwork. You don’t want to miss this ending!

Green Lantern Corps #20 proves that sometimes the best way to prepare for a big superhero story is to let the characters breathe. Hampton uses that breathing room extremely well, giving us personality, humor, mythology, and plenty of questions before the next big storm arrives. This feels like a prologue done right, and I’m ready for what comes next!

There’s no rest for the weary as the GLC find out the hard way there’s some new sheriffs in space. Hampton orchestrates the drama flawless with such an ensemble cast. The art delivers a solid combo of quick action and more defined emotions fueling it. There’s no better time like the present to jump onboard with the Corps!

Overall, G. Willow Wilson’s “Black Cat #14” is arguably the most fun book in the “Queen in Black” event so far. Given what happens, I’m very anxious to see where this leads not just for Felicia, but for the event as a whole! The team truly worked their butts off to make this issue as spectacular as it is and they pulled it off in supreme style.

This is a very strong transitional issue as we get Black Cat interacting with other members of the Marvel universe she ordinarily wouldn't, all while staying true to her character and snarky attitude. The conversation with her and the AI was a highlight, and we never forget; even with all of the comedy in this issue, it never takes away the fact that the world hangs in the balance. This is a high-stakes mission, and Black Cat handles it the only way she knows how: with luck and nine lives.

On a larger scale, a series could be really interesting as a gradual emergence for Barbara Gordon. She could really slowly develop into much more interesting character if this particular storyline has its opportunity to play out. Her experience inside of prison could add to her understanding of the criminal underworld in Gotham. And this could allow her to be a little bit more of a harder adjective crime fighter for the city if she were to make it out and get back under the cowl as Batgirl. For the time being, however, it's just really fun to see her work.

This run just keeps pulling me in further and further. Each issue has me on the edge of my seat wondering what will happen next. If you haven’t checked out Barbara Gordon: Breakout yet, be sure to include it on your pull list!

Punisher #8 keeps "Big Guns" moving with a grotesque helping of Deadpool weirdness and Punisher violence. Benjamin Percy continues to make Frank the quiet, increasingly irritated presence opposite Wade's constant commentary, a dynamic that works especially well once Blind Al enters the picture. The arrival of two major weapons pushes the larger story forward, although the central villain remains distant enough that the main conflict still feels like it's waiting to fully ignite. Jose Luis Soares and the art team make up for that with some wonderfully disgusting mini-Deadpools and the kind of brutal violence this crossover demands.

Punisher #8 sends Deadpool into a SHIELD facility to steal a special weapon as a test, and the Punisher comes along for the ride. Benjamin Percy’s script leans almost entirely on Deadpool as an excuse to get Frank a new weapon, which feels like a bait-and-switch if you want a Punisher story. That said, the art team more than makes up for the gap with phenomenal art.

Absolute Superman #23 is hard hitting and intense as Kal-El is hunting Braniac, who is always ahead of him by mere seconds. The mind games mix into reality and pushes Superman in a way I don’t believe any of us have ever seen in a comic before. This issue will leave you sitting and thinking with your own thoughts and is one that should be talked about as one of the most powerful superhero issue of the year.

An unthinkable evil forces Superman to question his ethics while searching for Brainiac! Aaron challenges the soul of hope with a superb script. Ferreyra unlocks a wide array of responses to the troubles brought forth. A stunning look at the Intricacy of hope in the Absolute Universe.

To save Gotham City, Batman jumps into a fire raging out of control. Fraction lights the match with an incredible script. Scalera and Morey bring breathtaking action on each page. The Dark Knight has never seen a fight like this before.

Batman #13 is a bit of a fast paced issue, but nonetheless a joy to read. Sometimes the issues that go too fast feel lackluster. And other times, they're like this – where little happens narratively but the things that do happen are frankly so dang cool that it's absolutely worth it. As a result, my only true gripe is that if you're not interested in this event, I'd say this one's worth skipping. But if you are? Buckle up and enjoy the ride.

reason.snippet: Spawn '77 #1 is a fascinating alternate take on Spawn that gives Todd McFarlane's teenage creation a surprisingly grounded revenge story. Mark Spears' painted artwork is frequently astonishing, especially when Spawn or the supernatural elements take center stage, though its hyperrealistic approach can make characters and environments look awkward and stiff. The story leans heavily on familiar gang…
pros: Spears' painted Spawn imagery can be absolutely stunning
The supernatural mystery adds an intriguing wrinkle to this version of Spawn
Plenty of locations and scene changes keep the 50-plus pages moving
cons: Characters occasionally have a stiff, dated quality
Some environments look sparse compared to the detailed character work
The gangster characters lean heavily on familiar tropes

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: ThunderCats: Cheetara #1 has a lot going for it. Maybe a little too much.
pros: Cheetara is a refreshingly level-headed protagonist.
Saladin Ahmed's third-person narrative captions give the book a unique feel.
The artwork by Andrea Arcari does a good job of capturing the dynamism of the heroine.
cons: While the narrative captions add a lot, there are places where they overstay their welcome.
The color art makes the book feel bland.

reason.snippet: Challenges of Doom: Spider-Man #1 will make readers see Spider-Man and Doctor Doom in a new light, adding layers to their first meeting.
pros: Ewing adds more layers to Spidey and Doom's first meeting.
Messina knows how to draw some great Spidey action, including a splash page where the web-slinger survives a massive explosion.
The final pages add more context to one of Doom's recurring rivalries, and it's not with the Fantastic Four.
One of the best Spider-Man moments I've read in a long time.

pros: Ties into the events of Queen in Black, yet can also serve as a standalone story.
Though the story might be in space, Wilson still keeps plenty of the wit and heists that's defined this series.
Melnikov has a gift for drawing sci-fi imagery.
cons: A missed chance to build upon Felicia and Sue Storm's newly forged friendship.

Ryan North spends much of the issue making that alternate existence feel genuinely happy and fulfilling, which gives the eventual turn tremendous weight. Francesco Mobili's double-page layouts beautifully convey entire stre…

North makes Doom's happiness convincing, strengthening the eventual turn
cons: Much of the issue is deliberately quiet compared to previous installments

I liked the design of the heroes in the book and look forward to seeing more of them.
